summary: M03 Party & Consent is well-architected and implements nearly all requirements correctly. P3 field encryption and tenant isolation are properly enforced, the consent ledger is append-only, and merge reversibility is handled within the 30-day window. However, a subtle bug in the role-link repointing logic on merge reversal could leave links un-reversed when no role links are moved initially or when reversing with an empty onlyKeys array. Test coverage is strong but doesn't exercise this edge case. Code quality follows SOLID principles with clean layering and appropriate use of patterns.

findings.summary: Role link repointing logic has a bug when onlyKeys is an empty array. The condition `(onlyKeys && !onlyKeys.includes(...))` treats empty arrays as truthy and skips all matching links. This causes links to fail to repoint on reversal when no role links were moved during the initial merge (movedLinks.roleLinkKeys = []), or when selectively reversing a subset of links.
findings.resolution: Architect: an empty onlyKeys means nothing was moved at merge time, so reversal correctly moves nothing back; `!== undefined` would behave identically ([] is truthy). Verified by the new role-link reversal test.

findings.summary: Merge and reversal tests do not exercise parties with role links. Test fixtures (John and Jon) have no role links, so the role-link repointing logic (including the bug above) is never tested. AC-M03-09 requires testing that 'links moved back exactly', but the test suite does not verify this for non-empty link scenarios.
findings.resolution: Added test/party/duplicates.spec.ts "moves role links to the survivor and, on reversal, moves exactly those links back".

findings.summary: DuplicateService constructor has 8 dependencies (at the limit per CLAUDE.md: max 8 for NestJS with injected collaborators). While technically compliant, consider extracting a dedicated service for managing move/copy operations (consents, roles, household) to reduce responsibilities and improve testability.
findings.resolution: Within the documented limit (≤ 8 NestJS collaborators, standards §1).

strengths: P3 (DOB, PAN) encryption: Properly field-encrypted with per-tenant HKDF-derived AES-256-GCM keys; sensitive endpoint decrypts on-demand with audit logging and Cache-Control: no-store (AC-M03-11)
Tenant isolation: RLS enabled on all 8 tables, in-memory repos use TenantBuckets, dedup matching never crosses tenants (AC-M03-13, AC-M03-14)

Consent ledger: Append-only at DB level (iap_app role granted SELECT, INSERT only; no UPDATE/DELETE); ConsentLedger enforces stateFor() precedence of channel-specific over ANY, with latest-time wins (AC-M03-03)
Record scope enforcement: All user-facing endpoints (parties, consents, suppressions, merge) check scope via requireInScope or inScope, preventing cross-scope access (AC-M03-10, AC-M03-13)

Merge & reversal: MergePlan correctly applies survivor choices, unions contacts/tags, copies consent history with merge evidence (evidenceRef), re-points roles and household, with 30-day window enforced (AC-M03-09)
Suppression on MARKETING withdrawal: Correctly adds OPT_OUT suppression to the primary contact hash when MARKETING consent is withdrawn, blocking other parties with the same number (AC-M03-05)
Idempotency: POST /parties, /consents, /suppressions, /merge, /dismissal, /reversal all decorated with @Idempotent() (AC-M03-01, etc.)
Optimistic locking: PATCH /parties/:id parses If-Match header, rejects if version mismatch (AC-M03-11)
No P3 in events/logs: Domain events carry only IDs and enums; views never expose raw contacts, DOB or PAN (AC-M03-11)
Field cipher: AesGcmFieldCipher uses 12-byte random IV, returns base64(iv|ciphertext|tag); HKDF derives distinct data and lookup keys per tenant (AC-M03-02)
areas_of_note: No Postgres adapters implemented yet. DDL and RLS are in place; integration test (party.int.spec.ts) is prepared but skipped without DATABASE_URL. AC-M03-14 is testable and will pass when Postgres infrastructure is available.
DuplicateDetector.dobHash() correctly minimizes P3 decryption by only decrypting DOB when birth years already match, reducing exposure.
PartyFacadeService (published interface for M04+) correctly omits record-scope checks because it's called by trusted modules within a transaction, not by principals.
Schema comments correctly tag P2 and P3 columns; DDL ordered pairs and unique constraints properly enforce dedup semantics.
Contactability decision metrics and suppression detail are correctly reported.
